fields.statement: QA at 5074bbfb with a binary built from the branch, in a fresh git repo after rhiza init and rhiza change new: ran docs/concepts/model.md's commands as written (rhiza add capability export-csv --field statement=..., rhiza set export-csv --field acceptance=..., rhiza add decision csv-streaming --field statement=..., rhiza link export-csv decided-by csv-streaming); each wrote an entry and rhiza show export-csv listed both fields and the decided-by link. go test -trimpath ./internal/doclinks/... passes, and rhiza check on a clean clone at the branch head prints ok with no docs-commands finding. Owner approval is left to the run's sign-off.

QA at 5074bbfb with a binary built from the branch, in a fresh repo: ran docs/concepts/change-sets.md's new block (add capability, add decision, link decided-by, set acceptance) in the current change set opened by rhiza change new; all four wrote into it. Checked the surrounding claims by hand: --change <id> wrote into the named change set rather than the current one, RHIZA_CHANGE did the same, a plain write went to the current one, and rhiza change use switched it back. go test -trimpath ./internal/doclinks/... passes; rhiza check on a clean clone at the branch head prints ok. Owner approval is left to the run's sign-off.

QA at 5074bbfb with a binary built from the branch, in a fresh repo: ran docs/concepts/why.md's decision block as written (rhiza add decision with a multi-line --field statement and a single-quoted --field quote containing double quotes, then rhiza link export-csv decided-by); rhiza show printed the quote verbatim with its quotes and the decides link. rhiza source add <handle> <file> --raw <file> added a source node as the page describes, and the rhiza-scrub skill the page points to exists. go test -trimpath ./internal/doclinks/... passes; rhiza check on a clean clone at the branch head prints ok. Owner approval is left to the run's sign-off.
